long_form.title_primary: How Nikola Faked a Truck and Lost $34 Billion
title_challengers: The Truck That Rolled Downhill and Cost $34 Billion
Trevor Milton Rolled a Truck Into Federal Prison
long_form.description:
Nikola was worth $34 billion and had never sold a single truck. Its most famous proof — a semi "in motion" — hid something the camera was angled to keep off screen.

This is the autopsy of a company that decided looking real was easier than being real. Trevor Milton unveiled a hydrogen-electric truck he said would end diesel, landed a partnership with GM, and watched retail investors pile into NKLA — all before the truck could move under its own power. Then a short-seller's report, the SEC, and a federal jury caught up with the one shortcut that started it.

primary.concept: Proof-of-human hybrid: real photo of Trevor Milton, closed-mouth grim expression, pushed to the left third against a black field (>50% negative space). Behind/right, a red downward arrow traces a subtle slope with a small semi-truck silhouette coasting down it. Red accent only; black/white/red palette. Delivers the 'the truck couldn't move on its own' promise without restating the money or prison beat.

challengers.concept: Artifact-focus variant pairing with the 'Truck That Rolled Downhill' title. Single Nikola semi on a red-outlined incline, a downhill gravity-vector arrow, and a power/ignition symbol crossed out in red. No face — the truck is the signature object. Black field, >50% negative space, red accent. Tests the mystery-object angle against the named-antagonist angle.

Downfall variant pairing with the 'Trevor Milton Into Federal Prison' title. Split composition: real photo of Milton (grim, closed-mouth) against black on one side; a stark courthouse/prison-corridor graphic on a red wash on the other. Red accent, minimal, >50% negative space. Tests the personal-consequence framing.

long_form.pinned_comment: Here's the part that still gets me: Nikola's engineers were actually building real hydrogen trucks — Milton just couldn't wait for them to be ready. If the real product was months away, why fake it? What do you think made him roll that truck down the hill instead of holding on?
